quick_review.text: 247 CMR 9.01(1): a licensee shall conduct professional activities in conformity with M.G.L. c. 112, §§ 24 through 42D, M.G.L. c. 94C, and 247 CMR 2.00: Definitions.

247 CMR 9.01(2): a licensee may not process a prescription, dispense a drug, device or other substance, or administer a controlled substance or vaccine in a manner intended, either directly or indirectly, to circumvent any law or regulation governing the practice of pharmacy.
The element that does the work in 247 CMR 9.01(2) is intention, and the paragraph expressly includes circumvention intended indirectly.
247 CMR 9.01(5): unless otherwise permitted by law, regulation, or Board policy, a licensee may not re-dispense any medication which has been previously dispensed.
247 CMR 9.01(9): a licensee may not engage in any fraudulent or deceptive act; the paragraph states no further condition.
247 CMR 9.03: a licensee may not engage in any advertising that is false, deceptive, or misleading, and the three descriptions are alternatives.
247 CMR 9.01(10): a licensee may not in any way aid or abet the unlawful practice of pharmacy.

247 CMR 9.01(11) runs both ways: a licensee may not offer, solicit, or receive remuneration or anything of value to or from a person who owns, operates, manages, or is an employee of a hospital, nursing home, or other health care facility.

The exchange in 247 CMR 9.01(11) must be in return for a referral to a pharmacy, pharmacist, pharmacy technician, or pharmacy intern, or for the generation of business from sale or furnishing of drugs, devices, or services to those persons or institutions; no individual referral is needed for the second limb.
Under 247 CMR 2.00 a person includes a corporation or any other legal entity, and a practitioner is any person with prescriptive privileges as defined in M.G.L. c. 94C, § 1.
247 CMR 9.01(14): a licensee may not provide any practitioner with blank prescription forms which refer to any pharmacist or pharmacy, whether or not anything is paid, agreed or steered.

247 CMR 9.01(12): a licensee may not dispense or distribute expired, outdated, defective, contaminated, counterfeit, contraband, or otherwise substandard drugs or devices to a person or entity not licensed or legally authorized to receive such drug or device.

The 247 CMR 9.01(12) test is the recipient's license or legal authorization, not the purpose of the transfer or any disclosure, and a licensed or legally authorized recipient is outside the prohibition.

247 CMR 9.01(13): unless otherwise permitted by law, a pharmacist connected with, or employed by, a hospital or clinic pharmacy without a Drug Store pharmacy license may dispense drugs only to the institution's inpatients or outpatients, its employees, and employees' spouses and children who live in the same household with them.

247 CMR 9.01(18): a pharmacist, pharmacy intern, and pharmacy technician carry, post on the wall of the pharmacy where he or she works, or have readily available at that pharmacy a license issued by the Board.
247 CMR 9.01(19): a pharmacist's name tag shows at least the first name and the title "Pharmacist", "Registered Pharmacist", or "R.Ph.".
247 CMR 9.01(20): a pharmacist maintains an NABP e-profile number, NABP being the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy.
247 CMR 9.01(21): a pharmacist complies with all elements of a drug's FDA required REMS, including any distribution or dispensing restriction included in its REMS.

URAMP rests on M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G, which requires the department of public health to establish a voluntary monitoring program for licensed health care professionals who seek support for mental health or substance use or are referred by a licensing board.

Admission requires specifying the condition or substance use and agreeing to comply with an individualized rehabilitation plan; the committee evaluates a request within 5 business days and the director admits eligible professionals.

Upon admission the licensing board may dismiss a pending investigation or complaint that arises from or relates to the mental health or substance use, and may change public license status to reflect non-disciplinary restrictions or conditions.

The URAMP manual describes non-disciplinary restriction status, with no practice, from receipt of the application, and dismissal without prejudice of related pending complaints on effective enrollment; it also describes a return to practice during participation once the program restores privileges, normally after six months of compliance under a substance use disorder agreement.

Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G(d)(2)(iv) the rehabilitation evaluation committee recommends whether a participant may continue or resume practice within the full scope of the license, and under § 65G(e) restrictions or conditions on practice, and changes to them, need the licensing board's approval.

On notice of withdrawal before completion or termination, the licensing board may immediately suspend the license as necessary to protect the public; the manual states that withdrawal leads the board to proceed with discipline on the underlying complaint.

The record of participation is not a public record and is not subject to subpoena or discovery without prior written consent, but a licensing board may use it as evidence where a professional it referred fails to complete the application, and the director reports name and license number to the board in board-referred or complaint-related cases.
On the committee's determination of successful completion the records are sealed, and the records of participation are destroyed 3 years after the date of successful completion.

The Board's former Pharmacy Substance Use Disorder Program transitioned to URAMP in December 2024; M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G(b)(2) directs a board with a similar statutory program duty, such as that in § 24H, to fulfill it by formally adopting the department's program.

decision_logic.condition: Money, gifts, hospitality or anything else of value passes, or is offered or requested, between a licensee and someone connected with a hospital, nursing home or other health care facility.
decision_logic.action: Test 247 CMR 9.01(11): identify an offer, solicitation or receipt; confirm that the other party owns, operates, manages, or is an employee of such a facility; and ask whether the value is in return for a referral to a pharmacy, pharmacist, pharmacy technician, or pharmacy intern, or for the generation of business from furnishing drugs, devices, or services to those persons or institutions. Do not look for cash, a named patient or a threshold of value.

decision_logic.condition: A licensee provides prescription forms to a prescriber.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether the forms are blank prescription forms, whether they refer to any pharmacist or pharmacy, and whether the recipient is a practitioner. If so, 247 CMR 9.01(14) forbids providing them, with no inquiry into payment, agreement or steering.

decision_logic.condition: Expired, outdated, defective, contaminated, counterfeit, contraband or otherwise substandard drugs or devices are to leave the pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Identify each recipient and ask whether it is licensed or legally authorized to receive such drug or device under the law that governs it. If it is not, 247 CMR 9.01(12) forbids dispensing or distributing to it, whatever the purpose or disclosure.

decision_logic.condition: A patient asks to be dispensed product that is expired or otherwise substandard.
decision_logic.action: Take the safe course and do not dispense it: 247 CMR 9.01(12) names dispensing among the forbidden acts, and nothing in it treats a prescription as authority to receive substandard product.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist connected with a hospital or clinic pharmacy is asked to dispense to someone.
decision_logic.action: Confirm whether that pharmacy holds a Drug Store pharmacy license; if it does, 247 CMR 9.01(13) does not apply. If it does not, dispense only to the institution's inpatients or outpatients, its employees, and employees' spouses and children who live in the same household with them, unless other law permits dispensing to someone else.

decision_logic.condition: A plan achieves through several steps, each lawful-looking on its own, what could not lawfully be done directly.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether a prescription is being processed, a drug, device or other substance dispensed, or a controlled substance or vaccine administered in a manner intended, directly or indirectly, to circumvent a law or regulation governing the practice of pharmacy. If so, 247 CMR 9.01(2) applies however each step looks alone.

decision_logic.condition: A record, statement or arrangement is designed to leave a false impression.
decision_logic.action: Treat it under 247 CMR 9.01(9) as a possible fraudulent or deceptive act without waiting for evidence of reliance, loss, gain or another broken rule.

decision_logic.condition: A licensee proposes an advertisement or promotional claim.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether it is false, whether it is deceptive and whether it is misleading. If any one of the three is true, 247 CMR 9.03 forbids a licensee to engage in it.

decision_logic.condition: A medication that has been previously dispensed is proposed for dispensing again.
decision_logic.action: Apply 247 CMR 9.01(5): do not re-dispense it unless a law, regulation, or Board policy permits it. Whether the pharmacy had to or could accept the medication back is a separate question taught with returns.

decision_logic.condition: A licensee is asked to help another person carry on activities that may be the practice of pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Decide first, under the licensure and scope rules that govern that person, whether the practice would be unlawful. If it would, 247 CMR 9.01(10) forbids aiding or abetting it in any way.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist, pharmacy intern or pharmacy technician arrives for work.
decision_logic.action: Check 247 CMR 9.01(18): the license issued by the Board must be carried, posted on the wall of the pharmacy where the person works, or readily available at that pharmacy. For a pharmacist also check 247 CMR 9.01(19): a name tag with at least the first name and the title "Pharmacist", "Registered Pharmacist", or "R.Ph.".

decision_logic.condition: A drug with an FDA-required REMS is to be dispensed.
decision_logic.action: Comply with all elements of its REMS, including any distribution or dispensing restriction, because 247 CMR 9.01(21) makes that a Massachusetts duty of the pharmacist; what the REMS requires is a federal subject taught with Medication Guides and REMS.

decision_logic.condition: A licensee with a mental health or substance use concern wants help and no one has referred the licensee anywhere.
decision_logic.action: Point to URAMP. Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G a licensed health care professional may seek support directly; admission requires specifying the condition or substance use and agreeing to comply with an individualized rehabilitation plan.

decision_logic.condition: A URAMP applicant or participant has a pending complaint.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether the complaint arises from or relates to the mental health or substance use. If it does, the licensing board may dismiss it upon admission, and the manual describes dismissal without prejudice on effective enrollment; if it does not, § 65G(g) supplies no power to dismiss it.

decision_logic.condition: A URAMP participant is considering withdrawing.
decision_logic.action: Expect that on the director's notice the licensing board may immediately suspend the license as necessary to protect the public, that the manual states the board will proceed with disciplinary action on the underlying complaint, and that the consent agreement records an agreement to surrender the license voluntarily on withdrawal.

decision_logic.condition: Someone seeks URAMP participation records by subpoena or in discovery.
decision_logic.action: The record of participation is confidential and not subject to subpoena or discovery in any civil, criminal, legislative or administrative proceeding without the participant's or applicant's prior written consent; separately, a licensing board may use it as evidence where a professional it referred failed to complete the application process.

ma_vs_federal.text: 247 CMR 9.01(21) is a Massachusetts regulation that requires a pharmacist to comply with all elements of a drug's FDA required REMS, including any distribution or dispensing restriction included in its REMS. The REMS itself is federal, and what it requires is taught with Medication Guides and REMS; in Massachusetts the pharmacist answers for compliance with it under the Board's practice standards as well.

exceptions.text: 247 CMR 9.01(13) opens with unless otherwise permitted by law, so its recipient list yields where other law permits dispensing to someone else, and a hospital or clinic pharmacy holding a Drug Store pharmacy license is outside the paragraph.
247 CMR 9.01(5) yields where law, regulation, or Board policy otherwise permits re-dispensing a previously dispensed medication; the paragraph does not itself say which ones do.
247 CMR 9.01(12) does not reach a person or entity licensed or legally authorized to receive such drug or device; it forbids dispensing or distributing substandard product to anyone else.
247 CMR 9.01(11) states no exception, whether for small value, disclosure or arrangements described as marketing.
247 CMR 9.01(14) states no exception, and it applies without payment, agreement or steering.
247 CMR 9.01(2) reaches a manner that is intended to circumvent; an inadvertent departure from a rule is not what the paragraph describes, though it may break that rule.
247 CMR 9.01(18) is met in any one of three ways: carrying the license, posting it on the wall of the pharmacy where the person works, or having it readily available at that pharmacy.
Noncompliance with an individualized rehabilitation plan may result in termination from URAMP only if the plan states that noncompliance will result in termination.

The licensing board's power to dismiss upon URAMP admission reaches only a pending investigation or complaint that arises from or relates to the participant's mental health or substance use, and the statute states it as a power, not a duty.

URAMP confidentiality yields where a professional referred by a licensing board fails to complete the application process, in which case a licensing board may use the record as evidence in a disciplinary proceeding, and the bar on subpoena and discovery yields to the participant's or applicant's prior written consent.

The manual describes dismissal on effective enrollment as without prejudice, and states that on withdrawal the licensing board will proceed with disciplinary action in relation to the underlying complaint.

timing_deadlines.event: A request to participate in URAMP is received
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 5 business days of receipt of the request
timing_deadlines.consequence: The rehabilitation evaluation committee evaluates the professional and provides recommendations regarding admission.

timing_deadlines.event: An applicant starts the URAMP application process
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Effective enrollment within 90 days, which the URAMP director may extend
timing_deadlines.consequence: Under the program's terms the applicant is to be effectively enrolled within that period.

Under the program's terms the licensing board changes the license status to non-disciplinary restriction, and the applicant is not permitted to practice; the manual states that the status remains upon effective enrollment and describes practice resuming only once the program restores practice privileges.

Under the program's terms pending complaints based on facts related to the incidents that led to enrollment are dismissed by the licensing board without prejudice; the statute itself leaves dismissal of related matters to the board.

timing_deadlines.event: Return to practice during URAMP participation
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Normally after 6 months of successful compliance under a substance use disorder agreement; for a complaint based on mental health functioning, after a period determined by the admission evaluator and/or the rehabilitation evaluation committee
timing_deadlines.consequence: Under the program's terms practice privileges are restored by the program before practice resumes, under a supervisor agreement with quarterly supervisor employment reports; under M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G(e) any change to a restriction or condition on practice is subject to the licensing board's approval, and the manual describes the licensing board as giving final approval.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Five years, with an opportunity for early discharge at the three-year mark
timing_deadlines.consequence: Early discharge is described as an opportunity at three years within the five-year term.

timing_deadlines.event: The director gives notice that a participant has withdrawn before completion or has been terminated
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Immediately on receipt of the notice
timing_deadlines.consequence: The licensing board may suspend the participant's license as is necessary to protect the public health, safety and welfare.

timing_deadlines.event: The rehabilitation evaluation committee determines that a participant has successfully completed the program
timing_deadlines.consequence: The department, the program, the committee and the licensing board, if applicable, seal all records pertaining to the participation.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: 3 years following the date of successful completion
timing_deadlines.consequence: The records of participation are destroyed.

timing_deadlines.event: Transition of the Board's Pharmacy Substance Use Disorder Program to URAMP
timing_deadlines.timeframe: December 2024; the URAMP FAQ gives December 16, 2024
timing_deadlines.consequence: URAMP absorbed PSUD and manages all monitoring program participation.

forms_records.text: The blank prescription form is itself the object of 247 CMR 9.01(14): a blank prescription form that refers to any pharmacist or pharmacy may not be provided to any practitioner.

A dispensing record arranged to show an eligible recipient or a sequence of events that did not in fact occur can be the deceptive act under 247 CMR 9.01(9) and part of the manner of circumvention under 247 CMR 9.01(2); neither paragraph creates a record-keeping duty of its own.
Whether a hospital or clinic pharmacy holds a Drug Store pharmacy license decides whether 247 CMR 9.01(13) applies to the pharmacists connected with it.

The license issued by the Board is the document 247 CMR 9.01(18) requires a pharmacist, pharmacy intern and pharmacy technician to carry, post on the wall of the pharmacy where he or she works, or have readily available at that pharmacy.
A pharmacist's name tag carries at least the first name and the title "Pharmacist", "Registered Pharmacist", or "R.Ph." under 247 CMR 9.01(19).

The NABP e-profile number is the identifier a pharmacist maintains under 247 CMR 9.01(20); the NABP Number that 247 CMR 2.00 defines, a unique seven digit number issued by the National Council for Prescription Drug Programs, is a differently worded term.
The advertisement is the object of 247 CMR 9.03: a licensee may not engage in one that is false, deceptive, or misleading.

A professional who applies to URAMP, or is referred to it, specifies the mental health condition or substance use in a form and format set by the department of public health, and each participant receives a written individualized rehabilitation plan with requirements for supervision and surveillance.

The record of participation is the materials received and reviewed by the director, the rehabilitation evaluation committee or a licensing board in connection with an application and with a participant's progress and compliance; it is not a public record.

The director's reports to the licensing board in board-referred or complaint-related cases carry the applicant's or participant's name and license number, and cover failure to complete admission, admission, termination, withdrawal and the plan's practice restrictions or conditions with their basis.

The URAMP Consent Agreement for Participants is a legally binding document entered into as a condition of acceptance, effective when countersigned by URAMP staff, and includes the participant's agreement to surrender the license voluntarily on withdrawal or on termination for noncompliance.
Where URAMP admission is being considered as an alternative to discipline, the manual states that the applicant is asked to sign a legally binding agreement not to practice during that period.

The publicly-available license status is the visible trace of participation: the statute lets the licensing board change it to reflect non-disciplinary restrictions or conditions, and the manual describes a non-disciplinary restriction status published without the reasons.

role_duties.duty: Conduct professional activities in conformity with M.G.L. c. 112, §§ 24 through 42D, M.G.L. c. 94C, and 247 CMR 2.00: Definitions; re-dispense no previously dispensed medication unless law, regulation, or Board policy permits it; aid or abet the unlawful practice of pharmacy in no way; and engage in no advertising that is false, deceptive, or misleading.

Refrain from processing a prescription, dispensing a drug, device or other substance, or administering a controlled substance or vaccine in a manner intended, directly or indirectly, to circumvent any law or regulation governing the practice of pharmacy, and from engaging in any fraudulent or deceptive act.

Neither offer, solicit nor receive remuneration or anything of value to or from anyone who owns, operates, manages or is employed by a hospital, nursing home or other health care facility in return for referrals or business generation, and provide no practitioner with blank prescription forms that refer to any pharmacist or pharmacy.

Dispense or distribute expired, outdated, defective, contaminated, counterfeit, contraband or otherwise substandard drugs or devices to no person or entity that is not licensed or legally authorized to receive them.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist connected with, or employed by, a hospital or clinic pharmacy without a Drug Store pharmacy license
role_duties.duty: Dispense drugs only to the institution's inpatients or outpatients, its employees, and employees' spouses and children who live in the same household with them, unless other law permits dispensing to someone else.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist, pharmacy intern and pharmacy technician
role_duties.duty: Carry, post on the wall of the pharmacy where he or she works, or have readily available at that pharmacy a license issued by the Board.

Wear a name tag with at least the first name and the title "Pharmacist", "Registered Pharmacist", or "R.Ph."; maintain an NABP e-profile number; and comply with all elements of a drug's FDA required REMS, including any distribution or dispensing restriction included in it.
Establish the voluntary program for monitoring the rehabilitation of licensed health care professionals and employ its program director.

Admit eligible professionals who request to participate, provide each participant a written individualized rehabilitation plan, terminate for noncompliance where the plan so states or for material misrepresentations, and in board-referred or complaint-related cases report name and license number to the licensing board on the listed events.

Evaluate requests to participate within 5 business days and recommend on admission, on continuing or resuming practice within the full scope of the license and on the individualized rehabilitation plan, and determine successful completion, which is followed by sealing of the records.

role_duties.role: Licensing board (for a license or registration issued by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy, that Board)
role_duties.duty: Decide whether to dismiss a related pending investigation or complaint on admission, change the publicly-available license status to reflect non-disciplinary restrictions or conditions, approve practice restrictions or conditions and changes to them, and suspend immediately where necessary on notice of withdrawal or termination.

Specify the mental health condition or substance use and agree to comply with the individualized rehabilitation plan; under the program's terms, admit to having problems with substance use and/or accept that mental health is currently impacting practice, waive all rights to appeal, file grievances or complaints, and contest licensure actions relating to or arising from participation, sign the consent agreement, refrain from practice while the non-disciplinary restriction status applies and until the program restores practice privileges, and on a return to practice work under a supervisor agreement with quarterly supervisor employment reports and obtain the program coordinator's written approval before practicing in a new practice setting.

Fulfill its statutory duty under M.G.L. c. 112, § 24H to establish a rehabilitation program for registered pharmacists, pharmacy interns and pharmacy technicians who have a substance use issue by formally adopting the department's program in lieu of establishing its own, as § 65G(b)(2) provides.

common_traps.text: Merging the provisions. Each paragraph of 247 CMR 9.01 taught here, and 247 CMR 9.03, has its own addressee, its own act and any exception of its own; among the prohibitions, words of permission appear only in paragraph (13), unless otherwise permitted by law, and paragraph (5), unless otherwise permitted by law, regulation, or Board policy.
Reading 247 CMR 9.01(2) as limited to the Board's own regulations or to direct circumvention. It reaches any law or regulation governing the practice of pharmacy, circumvented directly or indirectly.
Checking each step of an arrangement for lawfulness and stopping there. 247 CMR 9.01(2) looks to a manner intended to circumvent.
Reading 247 CMR 9.01(5) as absolute. It yields where law, regulation, or Board policy permits re-dispensing.
Looking for a victim before finding a deceptive act. 247 CMR 9.01(9) names no requirement of reliance, loss or gain, and no companion violation.
Reading 247 CMR 9.03 as reaching only false advertising. Advertising that is deceptive or misleading is within it too.
Treating non-cash benefits as outside 247 CMR 9.01(11). The paragraph reaches remuneration or anything of value, whether offered, solicited or received.

Requiring an individual patient referral under 247 CMR 9.01(11). The generation of business from furnishing drugs, devices, or services to facility-connected persons or institutions is a limb of its own.
Importing a remuneration element into 247 CMR 9.01(14). Free blank prescription forms that refer to a pharmacy are forbidden as much as paid-for ones.
Deciding 247 CMR 9.01(12) by the purpose of the transfer. Charity, training and disclosure do not substitute for a recipient licensed or legally authorized to receive such drug or device.
Reading 247 CMR 9.01(12) as a ban on all movement of expired stock. A recipient licensed or legally authorized to receive it is outside the prohibition.
Extending the family limb of 247 CMR 9.01(13) to parents or siblings, or to spouses and children who live elsewhere. It names spouses and children who live in the same household with the employee.
Treating the institution's own prescriber as a reason to dispense under 247 CMR 9.01(13). The list is defined by the recipient.
Reading 247 CMR 9.01(18) as requiring the license to hang on the wall. Carrying it, or having it readily available at the pharmacy where the person works, also meets the paragraph.
Treating a degree as a title under 247 CMR 9.01(19). The name tag needs at least the first name and one of the titles "Pharmacist", "Registered Pharmacist", or "R.Ph.".

Confusing the NABP e-profile number in 247 CMR 9.01(20) with the differently worded NABP Number that 247 CMR 2.00 defines as a seven digit number issued by the National Council for Prescription Drug Programs.

Treating REMS compliance as a purely federal matter. 247 CMR 9.01(21) makes compliance with all elements of a drug's REMS, including distribution and dispensing restrictions, a Massachusetts duty of the pharmacist.

Treating URAMP admission as automatic dismissal of every complaint. The licensing board may dismiss a pending matter that arises from or relates to the mental health or substance use, and the manual describes dismissal on effective enrollment as without prejudice.
Believing a licensee can reach URAMP only through a Board referral. A licensed health care professional may also seek support directly.

Treating URAMP confidentiality as absolute. The statute allows evidentiary use where a board-referred professional fails to complete the application, disclosure with prior written consent, and the director's reports of name and license number to the licensing board.

Assuming a participant can walk away without consequence. On notice of withdrawal or termination the licensing board may immediately suspend the license, and the manual states that the board will proceed with discipline on the underlying complaint.

Assuming a URAMP participant stays out of practice for the whole agreement. The committee recommends whether a participant may continue or resume practice, restrictions and changes need the licensing board's approval, and the manual describes privileges restored by the program, normally after six months of compliance under a substance use disorder agreement.

Treating PSUD as a separate pharmacy program still running. It transitioned to URAMP in December 2024, and § 65G(b)(2) directs a board with such a statutory duty to fulfill it by formally adopting the department's program.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G(b)(1) requires the department of public health to establish a voluntary program for monitoring the rehabilitation of licensed health care professionals who seek support for their mental health or substance use or who are referred to the program by a licensing board; § 65G was inserted by St. 2022, c. 177, § 36. Under § 65G(a) a licensed health care professional is an individual who holds a license, a license is a license, registration, authorization or certificate issued by a board of registration, and a licensing board is a board of registration that has issued a license; boards of registration include those serving in the department under M.G.L. c. 13, § 9, other than the board of registration established under c. 13, § 10, and M.G.L. c. 13, § 9(a) names the board of registration in pharmacy among the boards serving in the department of public health. Under § 65G(e) the department employs a program director who shall admit eligible licensed health care professionals who request to participate, provide each participant with a written individualized rehabilitation plan with requirements for supervision and surveillance, and terminate a participant based on noncompliance with that plan or material misrepresentations concerning the participant's participation in the program or professional practice; any restriction or condition relating to a participant's professional practice required under § 65G(e), and any change to one, is subject to the approval of the participant's licensing board. Under § 65G(d)(2) a rehabilitation evaluation committee appointed by the commissioner evaluates licensed health care professionals who request to participate within 5 business days of receipt of the request and provides recommendations regarding admission, and makes recommendations on whether a participant may continue or resume professional practice within the full scope of the license and on an individualized rehabilitation plan. Under § 65G(f) a licensed health care professional who applies to participate in or is referred by the licensing board to the program shall specify, in a form and format set by the department, the mental health condition or substance use that they believe may impede or has affected their ability to safely practice their profession, and shall agree to comply, to the best of their ability, with an individualized rehabilitation plan to be admitted; noncompliance with the plan may result in termination from the program only if the plan states that noncompliance will result in termination. Under § 65G(g), upon admission the licensing board may dismiss any pending investigation or complaint against the participant that arises from or relates to the participant's mental health or substance use, may change the participant's publicly-available license status to reflect the existence of non-disciplinary restrictions or conditions, and may immediately suspend the participant's license as is necessary to protect the public health, safety and welfare upon receipt of notice from the director that the participant has withdrawn from the program before completion or that the director has terminated the participant from the program.
exceptions: Noncompliance with an individualized rehabilitation plan may result in termination only if the plan states that noncompliance will result in termination

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G(a) the record of participation is the materials received and reviewed by the program's director, rehabilitation evaluation committee or a licensing board in connection with a licensed health care professional's application for admission and with a participant's progress and compliance with an individualized rehabilitation plan. Under § 65G(h) the record of participation shall not be a public record and is exempt from disclosure under clause Twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4 and chapter 66. If a licensed health care professional referred to the program by a licensing board fails to complete the application process, a licensing board may use information and documents in the record of participation as evidence in a disciplinary proceeding as necessary to protect public health, safety and welfare; in all other instances the record of participation or application to the program shall be kept confidential and shall not be subject to subpoena or discovery in any civil, criminal, legislative or administrative proceeding without the prior written consent of the participant or applicant. Upon the rehabilitation evaluation committee's determination that a participant has successfully completed the program and that the participant's ability to safely practice is not impaired or affected by mental health or substance use, the department, the program, the committee and the licensing board, if applicable, shall seal all records pertaining to the participant's participation, and the records of participation of participants who successfully complete the program shall be destroyed 3 years following the date of successful completion. Under § 65G(e)(viii), where an applicant or participant is referred to the program by a licensing board, or is the subject of a pending or completed investigation or complaint that arises from or relates to the applicant's or participant's mental health or substance use, the director shall report to the licensing board the name and license number of the applicant or participant in the event of the applicant's failure to complete the admission process, the participant's admission, termination or withdrawal before completion, and the initial restrictions or conditions relating to professional practice in the individualized rehabilitation plan together with any changes to or removal of them and the basis for them.
exceptions: A licensing board may use information and documents in the record of participation as evidence in a disciplinary proceeding, as necessary to protect public health, safety and welfare, where a professional referred by a licensing board fails to complete the application process
The bar on subpoena and discovery yields to the prior written consent of the participant or applicant

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The Unified Recovery and Monitoring Program's published pages state the following program terms. The program's overview page describes URAMP as a confidential, voluntary recovery and monitoring program for the boards and professions overseen by the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure, and states that the rehabilitation programs of a similar nature the Bureau previously established for the Board of Registration in Nursing (SARP) and the Board of Registration in Pharmacy (PSUD) transitioned to URAMP when it launched in December 2024. The URAMP Frequently Asked Questions page describes URAMP as a statewide unified recovery and monitoring program available to all healthcare professionals licensed by the Bureau, with applications available where they seek support for their mental health or substance use or are referred to the program by their licensing board. The URAMP Frequently Asked Questions page states that URAMP is established in accordance with Chapter 177 of the Acts of 2022, An Act Addressing Barriers to Care for Mental Health. The URAMP Guidance Manual defines URAMP as the program developed and governed by the Massachusetts Bureau of Health Professions Licensure, a structured program designed to assist licensed health care professionals with substance use and functional impairment due to a mental health condition that impairs safe practice. The URAMP Frequently Asked Questions page gives December 16, 2024 as the date URAMP launches and as the date from which the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Pharmacy Substance Use Disorder Program (PSUD) and the Board of Registration in Nursing's Substance Addiction Recovery Program (SARP) transition to URAMP, which absorbs them, with all monitoring program participation managed by the URAMP team. It describes SARP and PSUD as confidential, voluntary programs for licensed healthcare professionals with substance use disorders that impact their practice, and URAMP as also a confidential, voluntary program, available as well to licensees with mental health concerns that are not related to substance use disorders and have the potential to impact their practice. An applicant obtains the application from URAMP staff by calling the confidential URAMP line, and shall be effectively enrolled within ninety days of starting the application process, a period the URAMP director may extend. Upon receipt of the application the applicant's license status is changed online by the licensing board to non-disciplinary restriction, meaning the applicant is not permitted to practice; that status is published in the licensee database without the reasons for it and remains upon effective enrollment. The manual describes URAMP as able to function as an alternative to disciplinary proceedings where evidence indicates that the incident happened as a result of, or in connection with, a substance use disorder or mental health condition, giving the licensee the opportunity to demonstrate, in a non-disciplinary and non-public manner, that the health condition can be managed so that the licensee can safely return to practice while retaining the license. When admission is being considered as an alternative to discipline the applicant is asked to sign a legally binding agreement not to practice during that period. While an application is pending the complaint resolution process continues, and where admission is not granted the case is remitted to the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure investigators to determine whether disciplinary proceedings are required. A referral by licensing board investigators may not mean entry into the program, and a referral is described as unlikely to be appropriate where a licensed health professional has diverted drugs for sale or distribution to others, caused harm to a patient because of their abuse, or engaged in behavior with a high potential for causing harm, such as substituting or tampering with patients' drugs. Applicants must admit to having problems with substance use and/or accept that mental health is currently impacting their practice, and agree to waive all rights to appeal, file grievances or complaints, and contest licensure actions relating to or arising from their URAMP participation. Participation is governed by the URAMP Consent Agreement for Participants, a legally binding document entered into as a condition of acceptance into the program, effective when countersigned by URAMP staff, by which the participant agrees to voluntarily surrender the license should the participant fail to successfully complete participation by withdrawal or by termination for noncompliance; a URAMP agreement runs five years with an opportunity for early discharge at the three-year mark. Upon effective enrollment, pending complaints based on facts related to the incidents that led to enrollment are dismissed by the licensing board without prejudice. A participant may withdraw at any point, and the licensing board will then proceed with disciplinary action in relation to the underlying complaint; noncompliance may result in a cease-to-practice order, an extension or modification of the agreement, termination from the program and a report to the licensing board; and at any point during participation the licensing board may obtain pertinent records of participation. Records pertaining to participation, including the application, are described as confidential and not subject to public records requests; participants admitted into URAMP are not reported in public or to any disciplinary database; participant matters heard before the rehabilitation evaluation committee and the licensing board are heard in executive session; and if an applicant decides not to participate after the application has been submitted, the information provided may be used by the licensing board in connection with a subsequent disciplinary action, only where it is relevant to the matter under investigation. When the licensing board has approved successful discharge, all URAMP records are sealed and any related complaints are dismissed, and upon successful completion program conditions end and the license status changes to current.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The URAMP Guidance Manual describes practice during participation as follows. It states that all admissions carry an out of practice consideration: participants entering URAMP for a complaint based on a substance use disorder normally require a restriction from practice for the first six months in the program, with gradual return to work privileges granted as they continue to meet the program compliance criteria, while the duration of the restriction from practice for a complaint based on mental health functioning is determined by the URAMP admission evaluator and/or the rehabilitation evaluation committee; for mental health admissions the manual states that the program avoids fixed standards, including the length of time away from work. Under the heading Return to Practice Requirements the manual states that practice privileges shall be restored by the program prior to returning to practice, that return to practice requires a supervisor agreement and quarterly supervisor employment reports, and that, if required by the agreement, one year of health professions practice is required to successfully discharge from the program. Under Application for UCAP Changes, a participant requests a change to the URAMP Consent Agreement for Participants in writing on the required form; changes are considered only once the participant has demonstrated compliance with all the agreement's provisions and documentation requirements and only at the timeframes the agreement specifies; all changes must be reviewed and approved by URAMP staff or the rehabilitation evaluation committee; and the requests listed as applicable to all participants include, normally, a return to practice after six months of successful compliance under a substance use disorder agreement, a return to practice after a period out of practice as determined by the admission evaluator and/or the committee, and the return of practice restricted privileges as outlined in each agreement. Under Management of Disciplinary Matters, Step Four, after pending related complaints are dismissed on effective enrollment the licensing board authorizes the URAMP director to change the license status in accordance with the terms of the agreement and URAMP's staff action policy. Under Confidentiality Upon Successful Completion of the Program, the manual states that the URAMP legislation requires any change to a licensing restriction or condition to be approved by the participant's licensing board, and that where URAMP staff or the committee has approved a return to practice, with or without restrictions, during or at the conclusion of the program, the recommendations are put before the licensing board for final approval, without the participant's personal identifiable information. A participant must receive written approval from the URAMP program coordinator before practicing in a new practice setting, and may request to be heard before the committee for reconsideration of practice restrictions that are a significant barrier to practicing where the organization can offset or accommodate the barrier.
exceptions: For a complaint based on mental health functioning the manual sets no fixed period out of practice; the admission evaluator and/or the rehabilitation evaluation committee determines the duration of the restriction.
